eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study applies deep learning to automate lung size measurements in adult lung transplant recipients but does not assess survival, waitlist mortality, complications, quality of life, or economic outcomes, thus failing the outcome criterion.

identification_methods.Setting: Single tertiary academic center (University of Pennsylvania)
identification_methods.Comments: Pilot study developing an AI system for automated lung size measurements from portable chest radiographs, validated on 50 transplant recipients.
identification_methods.Institution: Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania
identification_methods.Address: 3400 Spruce St, 6 Silverstein Pavilion, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Portable chest radiographs from lung transplant recipients at University of Pennsylvania; Darwin public CXR dataset for training
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included 50 lung transplant recipients; images selected to include technical challenges such as consolidations, effusions, and rotation.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: PSPNet segmentation model for lung mask extraction followed by computer‑vision feature point detection
identification_methods.Comparator: Measurements by two expert radiologists (blinded comparison)
identification_methods.Input Variables: Portable chest radiographs; derived lung masks; geometric feature points
identification_methods.Validation Method: Blinded comparison of AI measurements with radiologist measurements on 50 CXRs; linear regression calibration; Pearson correlation and intraclass correlation coefficients reported
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Data augmentation (rotation, scaling, translation) and contrast‑limited adaptive histogram equalization applied; model trained on 6500 Darwin CXRs with masks; validation performed on institutional CXR set.

population.Population Notes: Pilot study using portable chest radiographs of 50 recipients, including images with technical challenges.

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: PSPNet segmentation model with computer vision postprocessing
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Two-step framework: automatic lung segmentation using PSPNet trained on Darwin dataset with data augmentation, followed by computer‑vision feature point detection to compute six lung size measurements.
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Average measurement error, Pearson correlation coefficient, intraclass correlation coefficients between AI and radiologists
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Focus on accuracy and agreement of AI‑generated lung size measurements compared with expert radiologist readings.
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AI achieved <2.5% error (<7 mm), Pearson r=0.97, ICC >0.95 for all measurements.
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported name: Measurement error of AI‑generated lung size metrics
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: Average of two radiologist measurements (reference standard)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Percentage error and Pearson correlation coefficient
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Average absolute error percentage and Pearson correlation between AI measurements and radiologist reference on a held‑out test set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Demonstrated high agreement with expert radiologists despite challenging image conditions.
